alt_names: Anhalt-Dessau, Anhalt-Bernburg, Anhalt-Köthen and Anhalt-Zerbst (the lines)

successors.note: Cliopatria's Duchy of Anhalt row starts in 1806. The lines went extinct in 1853 (Köthen) and 1863 (Bernburg), merging into one duchy.

capitals.name: Dessau
capitals.note: The infobox lists Dessau as capital 'when united'; the lines resided at Dessau, Bernburg, Köthen and Zerbst.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Anhalt row before the 1806 Duchy). The page: 'The area of the later duchy was 906 sq mi (2,300 km2)' and names Dessau, Bernburg, Köthen, Zerbst, Plötzkau, Ballenstedt and Aschersleben. A 27 km circle at 12.00E 51.82N (about 2,290 km2) matches the later duchy; a 12 km circle at Aschersleben (11.46E 51.76N, about 450 km2) is the lands of the Aschersleben line, soft.

correction.text: Anhalt without Aschersleben: Dessau, Bernburg, Köthen, Zerbst and Plötzkau

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The family ruling in Aschersleben became extinct in 1315', and the district went to Halberstadt. The page dates the lines' divisions and reunions (1396, 1570, 1603, 1665, 1793) and none of them moves land out of Anhalt; one state is drawn throughout.

ledger.note: 1212: Anhalt. 'The Anhalt territory was split off the German stem duchy of Saxony in 1212' (Count Bernhard's heirs divided his lands that year; Bernhard had become Duke of Saxony in 1180).
1218: a prince. 'In 1218, Henry I assumed the title of a prince.'
1252: the first partition. 'On Henry's death in 1252, his three sons partitioned the principality' into Aschersleben, Bernburg and Zerbst. Entered as a dynastic step inside one state.

1315: Aschersleben. 'The family ruling in Aschersleben became extinct in 1315' and the district went to Halberstadt (the Halberstadt page: 'In 1315 the prince-bishop acquired the former Principality of Aschersleben').
1570: reunion. Joachim Ernest 'unite[d] the whole of Anhalt under his rule in 1570'.

1603: the mini-states. 'In 1603 it was split up into the mini states of Anhalt-Dessau, Anhalt-Bernburg' and others (Köthen, Zerbst, Plötzkau); Plötzkau was surrendered to Bernburg in 1665 when Köthen 'became extinct', and Zerbst was divided after Frederick Augustus died in 1793.
1806: duchies. 'In 1806, Napoleon elevated the remaining states of Anhalt-Bernburg, Anhalt-Dessau and Anhalt-Köthen to duchies'; Anhalt-Plötzkau and Anhalt-Zerbst 'had ceased to exist'.

certainty.note: The page gives the later duchy's area (2,300 km2) and town names, no boundary; the circle is a stand-in.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria's Duchy of Anhalt starts in 1806.

SCOPE. 1212 (Anhalt split off Saxony) to 1806 (elevation of the remaining lines to duchies). All lines are kept in one state: the page's partitions (1252, 1396 Zerbst split with Dessau and Kothen, 1562 Köthen surrendered to Dessau, 1570 reunion, 1603 mini-states, 1665 Köthen extinct, 1793 Zerbst) are dynastic steps. The page also dates Henry I's title (1218), Bernhard as Duke of Saxony (1180), Wolfgang of Köthen co-signing the Augsburg Confession (1530) and being put under the imperial ban after Mühlberg (1547), 'joined Council of Princes: 1582', and the Thirty Years' War ravages (undated); none moves land.

SHAPES. Anhalt 12.00E 51.82N 27 km; Aschersleben 11.46E 51.76N 12 km. The Aschersleben event mirrors the Halberstadt dossier of this batch (whose counterpart name is `principality-of-anhalt`). Gazetteer names wanted: 'Dessau', 'Bernburg', 'Köthen', 'Zerbst', 'Plötzkau', 'Aschersleben'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The page gives the Aschersleben line's extent no area; (2) no 1252 land per son; (3) the page gives no end year for the principality (it describes the duchies); 1806 is the year the page dates.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: none new.
